notes.tone: The rowdy human table and the most openly funny stop on the tour. Humour comes from the characters — greed, vanity, charm with a knife in it, a devil who is never in a hurry — never from outside the world. Rowdy, not crude.
notes.difficulty: Third table. The contempt is louder than at the White House and less polite: the player is a prisoner, and pirates say so. Nobody stays cruel for long — they respect anyone who can take a pot off them.
notes.dealer_plant: The single 'the dealer arranged it' line for this table is pc_plant_03. Do NOT add a second.
notes.blackbeard: Dominates the room from hand one: loud, theatrical, and fully aware that the legend is a performance he built on purpose. His one quiet line is the dealer plant, which is why it lands.
notes.davy_jones: FOLKLORE ONLY. Nothing from the Disney films: no 'Do you fear death?', no 'part of the crew, part of the ship', no wagering souls or years of service, no organ, no chest, no heart. He speaks rarely, briefly, and without raising his voice.
notes.silver: Stevenson's Silver, not Robert Newton's. No 'Arr'. He says 'shipmate' and 'Cap'n', and he talks to the parrot. Charming to everyone at once; loyal to whoever is winning.
notes.kidd: True history only. He insists to anyone who will listen that he was a privateer, not a pirate. The joke is that he is saying it at this table.
notes.no_dead_mans_chest: Do not use Stevenson's 'Dead Man's Chest' song at this table: it is public domain, but it is also the title of the Disney film that owns the tentacled Davy Jones.
notes.leak_rule: No line may reference hand strength while cards are live.
notes.voice: Champion (Blackbeard) + Death are voiced. Kidd/Silver/Davy Jones are text + vocalization. Captain Flint the parrot gets real squawks.

respect_tiers.0: Contempt. The player is a prisoner — cargo — and is not addressed by any name.
respect_tiers.1: Grudging notice. The crew gives the player a nickname: powder monkey.
respect_tiers.2: Real address. They speak TO the player, by name, as crew.
respect_tiers.3: Title. Earned. Blackbeard uses it first, and makes the room stand for it.

table_intro.speaker: death
table_intro.text: A tavern on a cove no chart admits to. The smoke is from the lamps, the pipes, and the gentleman in the corner's hat.

table_intro.speaker: death
table_intro.text: I have met three of them professionally. The cook got away.
table_intro.foreshadow: Reads as a joke about pirates coming to bad ends. Literally true: he was there when Kidd was hanged and when Blackbeard fell at Ocracoke, and Davy Jones is in the same trade. Silver escapes at the end of his book — the one man at this table Death has never collected.

table_intro.speaker: death
table_intro.text: Win, and you are crew. Lose, and you are ballast. Sit.

dealer_plant.speaker: kidd
dealer_plant.text: Who gave the prisoner a stake? I'll not split a prize with the cargo.

dealer_plant.speaker: silver
dealer_plant.text: Wasn't me, Captain. I'd remember. I'd have charged.

dealer_plant.speaker: blackbeard
dealer_plant.note: Said quietly, by the loudest man in the room. The drop in volume is the whole beat.

dealer_plant.speaker: kidd
dealer_plant.text: ...Well. Plenty of prize to go round, I suppose.
dealer_plant.note: THE SHRUG. From the greediest man at the table, which is how you know nobody questions the dealer. The player never gets an answer.

kidd_blackbeard.relationship: Kidd sailed with the King's commission to hunt pirates, was hanged as one in 1701, and insisted to the end he was a privateer. Blackbeard was the genuine article a generation later — and took the King's pardon in 1718, which Kidd was never offered. The respectable man they hanged, and the pirate they pardoned.

exchanges.speaker: kidd
exchanges.text: I'll have you know I sailed under the King's own commission.

exchanges.speaker: blackbeard
exchanges.text: And I held Charleston.

exchanges.speaker: kidd
exchanges.text: For a chest of medicine.

exchanges.speaker: blackbeard
exchanges.text: It was a very good chest.

exchanges.speaker: kidd
exchanges.text: They hanged me at Wapping to put the fear into men like you.

exchanges.speaker: blackbeard
exchanges.text: Did it work?

exchanges.speaker: kidd
exchanges.text: ...Evidently not.

exchanges.speaker: blackbeard
exchanges.text: You should have taken the King's pardon, Kidd. I did.

exchanges.speaker: kidd
exchanges.text: The King offered a pardon to every pirate in the Indies but two. I was one of the two.
exchanges.note: True: the royal proclamation of 1698 offering pardon to pirates in the East Indies excluded Kidd and Henry Every by name.

exchanges.speaker: blackbeard
exchanges.text: Ha! Who was the other?

exchanges.speaker: kidd
exchanges.text: Henry Every. He got away with it.

exchanges.speaker: blackbeard
exchanges.text: What did you do to your gunner, Kidd? I heard it was a bucket.

exchanges.speaker: kidd
exchanges.text: He called me a rogue.

exchanges.speaker: blackbeard
exchanges.text: And?

exchanges.speaker: kidd
exchanges.text: It was a very heavy bucket.
exchanges.note: True: Kidd struck his gunner William Moore with an iron-bound bucket in 1697 after an argument, and was hanged partly for it.

needles.speaker: blackbeard
needles.text: Folded, Kidd? That's the privateer in you.

needles.speaker: kidd
needles.text: Thank you.

needles.speaker: blackbeard
needles.text: It wasn't a compliment.

needles.speaker: kidd
needles.text: It was to me.

needles.speaker: kidd
needles.text: The great Blackbeard, folding. I'll have that entered in the log.

needles.speaker: blackbeard
needles.text: Write it small. Nobody reads a hanged man's log.

silver_blackbeard.relationship: Stevenson borrowed from the real record. In Treasure Island the Squire says 'Blackbeard was a child to Flint', and the coxswain Israel Hands is named after Blackbeard's own officer — the man Blackbeard shot in the knee. The one real pirate Silver's world measures itself against, and a cook who has never met a captain he would not sell.

exchanges.speaker: silver
exchanges.text: I've heard it said Blackbeard was a child to Flint.

exchanges.speaker: blackbeard
exchanges.text: Who's Flint?

exchanges.speaker: silver
exchanges.text: Ah. He'd have hated that most of all.

exchanges.speaker: blackbeard
exchanges.text: I had a man called Israel Hands. Shot him in the knee, under the table, so the crew wouldn't forget who I was.

exchanges.speaker: silver
exchanges.text: We had an Israel Hands. Coxswain. A boy shot him.

exchanges.speaker: blackbeard
exchanges.text: Unlucky name.

exchanges.speaker: silver
exchanges.text: [moves his chair a little further from Blackbeard's]

exchanges.speaker: blackbeard
exchanges.text: Whose side are you on, cook?

exchanges.speaker: silver
exchanges.text: Yours, Cap'n. Right up until I'm not, and you'll be the first to know.

exchanges.speaker: blackbeard
exchanges.text: Will I?

exchanges.speaker: silver
exchanges.text: ...Second.

exchanges.speaker: blackbeard
exchanges.text: Where did you leave your leg, cook?

exchanges.speaker: silver
exchanges.text: In the King's service, Cap'n. Lost it under the immortal Hawke.

exchanges.speaker: blackbeard
exchanges.text: Did you?

exchanges.speaker: silver
exchanges.text: It's a better story than the true one.
exchanges.note: Treasure Island, ch. 7: the Squire reports that Silver lost the leg 'in his country's service, under the immortal Hawke'. It is Silver's own account.

needles.speaker: blackbeard
needles.text: Changing sides again, cook?

needles.speaker: silver
needles.text: Never, Cap'n. Just stepping out of the line of fire. Different thing entirely.

needles.speaker: silver
needles.text: There, Cap'n Flint. Even Blackbeard strikes his colours to the cook.

needles.speaker: blackbeard
needles.text: Say that again and the bird goes in the stew.

needles.speaker: silver
needles.text: [tucks the parrot inside his coat]

davy_jones_table.relationship: Every sailor at this table has spent a life on the water with Davy Jones somewhere underneath it, and every one of them knows exactly where his locker is. He is patient with all of them. None of them enjoys that. Each exchange pairs him with one sailor — fire the one that matches who contested the pot.

exchanges.speaker: davy_jones
exchanges.text: Three tides washed over you at Wapping, Captain.

exchanges.speaker: kidd
exchanges.text: I recall.

exchanges.speaker: davy_jones
exchanges.text: I waited. They tarred you and hung you in a cage instead.

exchanges.speaker: kidd
exchanges.text: Everyone wanted their share of me. You and half the lords in London.

exchanges.speaker: blackbeard
exchanges.text: They say when they threw me over the side, I swam round the sloop before I went down.

exchanges.speaker: davy_jones
exchanges.text: They say.

exchanges.speaker: blackbeard
exchanges.text: Well? Did I?

exchanges.speaker: davy_jones
exchanges.text: You were very determined.

exchanges.speaker: silver
exchanges.text: Now, Mr. Jones. A gentleman in your line must be open to a bargain.

exchanges.speaker: davy_jones
exchanges.text: Everyone who comes down to me tries to bargain.

exchanges.speaker: silver
exchanges.text: Aye, but I'm good at it.

exchanges.speaker: davy_jones
exchanges.text: So you never came down.

exchanges.speaker: blackbeard
exchanges.text: Why do you never raise your voice, Jones?

exchanges.speaker: davy_jones
exchanges.text: I've never needed to. Everyone comes to me in the end.

exchanges.speaker: blackbeard
exchanges.text: Not me. Not yet.

exchanges.speaker: davy_jones
exchanges.text: No. Not yet.

exchanges.speaker: silver
exchanges.text: Mr Jones. What's it like, down there?

exchanges.speaker: davy_jones
exchanges.text: Quiet. Dark. Everyone's very honest.

exchanges.speaker: silver
exchanges.text: ...Doesn't sound like my sort of place at all.

exchanges.speaker: kidd
exchanges.text: Do you keep accounts down there, Jones?

exchanges.speaker: davy_jones
exchanges.text: Every sailor. Every ship.

exchanges.speaker: kidd
exchanges.text: Then you'll have the Quedagh Merchant on your books. I want a copy.

exchanges.speaker: davy_jones
exchanges.text: Everyone wants a copy.

needles.speaker: davy_jones
needles.text: Let go, Captain. It gets easier.

needles.speaker: kidd
needles.text: That's what they said at Wapping.

needles.speaker: davy_jones
needles.text: You let that one sink, Captain.

needles.speaker: blackbeard
needles.text: I let it drift. There's a difference.

needles.speaker: davy_jones
needles.text: Not to me.

needles.speaker: davy_jones
needles.text: Folded, cook.

needles.speaker: silver
needles.text: Aye. A man who knows when to leave a ship never goes down with one.

needles.speaker: davy_jones
needles.text: I'll wait.

needles.speaker: kidd
needles.text: Ha! The devil of the deep, backing water!

needles.speaker: davy_jones
needles.text: The tide goes out. It always comes in again.

needles.speaker: blackbeard
needles.text: Back to your locker, Jones!

needles.speaker: davy_jones
needles.text: After you, Captain. I insist.

silver_kidd.relationship: Treasure. Kidd is one of the very few pirates known to have really buried any — on Gardiners Island in 1699 — and the Governor had it dug up while Kidd sat in his gaol. Silver sailed for Flint's gold and found the pit already empty. Two men who got to the hole too late.

exchanges.speaker: silver
exchanges.text: Seven hundred thousand pound, Flint's gold. We found the pit already dug and one coin in the bottom.

exchanges.speaker: kidd
exchanges.text: Mine the Governor dug up while I sat in his gaol.

exchanges.speaker: silver
exchanges.text: There's no justice for a man who buries a thing.

exchanges.speaker: kidd
exchanges.text: None. I've looked.

exchanges.speaker: silver
exchanges.text: Between shipmates, Captain — where's the rest of it?

exchanges.speaker: kidd
exchanges.text: I offered to show them. If they'd let me live.

exchanges.speaker: silver
exchanges.text: And?

exchanges.speaker: kidd
exchanges.text: [rubs his neck]

exchanges.speaker: kidd
exchanges.text: What would you have done with Flint's gold, Silver?

exchanges.speaker: silver
exchanges.text: Set up gentleman. Ride in a coach. Sit in Parliament, maybe.

exchanges.speaker: kidd
exchanges.text: Parliament hanged me.

exchanges.speaker: silver
exchanges.text: Well, I'd have been on the other side of it, see.
exchanges.note: Kidd was examined before the House of Commons in 1701. Silver means to "set up gentleman in earnest" after the voyage (Treasure Island, ch. 11).

needles.speaker: silver
needles.text: No shame in it, Captain. A man can't dig every hole on the island.

needles.speaker: kidd
needles.text: Mine wasn't empty. They took it.

needles.speaker: kidd
needles.text: Folded, Silver? For once you picked a side and stayed on it.

needles.speaker: silver
needles.text: The side that folds, Captain. It's never once been hanged.

tier_0.speaker: blackbeard
tier_0.text: Somebody count what that one's got. I want to know what I'm taking.

tier_0.speaker: kidd
tier_0.text: Another hand in the prize. Put it down for half a share. Less.

tier_0.speaker: silver
tier_0.text: Sit you down. Cap'n Flint likes a newcomer. She's outlived a great many.

tier_0.speaker: blackbeard
tier_0.text: [sets a pistol on the table, pointed at nobody in particular]

tier_1.speaker: blackbeard
tier_1.text: Ha! The powder monkey's found a match.
tier_1.note: Announcement. The first time anyone at this table calls the player anything.

tier_1.speaker: silver
tier_1.text: Didn't I say so from the first, Cap'n Flint? I said so. Ask the bird.

tier_1.speaker: kidd
tier_1.text: Keep your hands off my share and we'll get along.

tier_2.speaker: kidd
tier_2.text: {name}. I'll write that into the articles myself. Properly, in ink.

tier_2.speaker: silver
tier_2.text: Between you and me, I always backed you. Told the others the same, mind — but I meant it with you.

tier_2.speaker: blackbeard
tier_2.text: Sit easy. Crew don't get shot. Not often.

tier_3.speaker: blackbeard
tier_3.text: On your feet, the lot of you. There's a Commodore at the table.
tier_3.note: First time anyone gives the player a title. Nobody at this table has ever stood for anyone but him.

tier_3.speaker: silver
tier_3.text: Commodore! Hear that, Cap'n Flint? Outranks you now.

tier_3.speaker: kidd
tier_3.text: If they ever offer you a commission, read every word of it.

tier_3.speaker: davy_jones
tier_3.text: Every voyage ends at the same table. Yours has further to sail than most.
tier_3.foreshadow: Reads as sailor's fatalism — every ship ends in the locker. Literally: every voyage, the player's tour included, ends at Death's table.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Take your time. The tide will not wait. I will.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: At sea, that is called weather.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: The last man to beat him needed two sloops, five pistol balls and twenty cuts. This was cheaper.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: The first one over the side. The sea does not keep count. I do.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Pirates usually put that sort of thing to a vote. You did not wait for one.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: That is a share worth hanging for. One of them did.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: The water is rising. It does that.

champion_headsup.speaker: blackbeard
champion_headsup.text: Just us, then. Let's make a little hell of our own, and see who can bear it longest.
champion_headsup.note: After the General History's story of Blackbeard shutting himself and his crew in the hold with pots of burning brimstone, to see who could stand it longest. He did.

champion_headsup.speaker: blackbeard
champion_headsup.text: I took the King's pardon once. It didn't take.

champion_headsup.speaker: blackbeard
champion_headsup.text: Most ships struck their colours the moment they saw who it was. You're still sitting there.

champion_headsup.speaker: blackbeard
champion_headsup.text: Ha! Do that again and I'll have to start taking you seriously.

kidd.speaker: kidd
kidd.text: I was a privateer. Put that on the gibbet.

kidd.speaker: kidd
kidd.text: Well. At least it only took the once this time.
kidd.note: At his hanging in 1701 the first rope broke, and he was hanged again.

silver.speaker: silver
silver.text: No hard feelings, shipmates. There never are, with me.

silver.speaker: silver
silver.text: Come along, Cap'n Flint. There's always a port with a boat in it.

davy_jones.speaker: davy_jones
davy_jones.text: No matter. I'll see most of you again.

davy_jones.speaker: davy_jones
davy_jones.text: There's no hurry. There's never any hurry, down there.

blackbeard.speaker: blackbeard
blackbeard.text: Ha! Well struck. Tell it bigger than it was.

blackbeard.speaker: blackbeard
blackbeard.text: Somebody see to my hat. I'll not go out without the smoke.

player_busted.speaker: blackbeard
player_busted.text: Over the side! ...Somebody throw a rope. I'm not done with that one.

player_busted.speaker: silver
player_busted.text: Never mind, shipmate. Come back with a fresh stake. I'll keep your seat warm — for a small consideration.

player_busted.speaker: death
player_busted.text: Not everyone the sea takes stays taken. Sit down again when you are dry.

champion_defeat.speaker: blackbeard
champion_defeat.text: Take the table. And when you tell it, put a storm in it, and make me ten feet tall.

champion_defeat.speaker: death
champion_defeat.text: Three. Five remain. I will tell it exactly as it was.
champion_defeat.note: Death does not embellish, even when asked to. Worth the player noticing: it is the key to reading every aside he makes.
